title: CFPB student-loan timing fields measure different institutional endpoints
source_unit: published CFPB student-loan complaint record in product-filtered API aggregations, grouped by calendar year received

observations.method: Official CFPB product-filtered API aggregation for student-loan complaints received in 2024; compare the company_response bucket with the separate timely bucket.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; fields are administrative classifications. This audit does not infer elapsed days, borrower harm, or remedy.
observations.counterinterpretation: The two fields may represent different processing stages or coding rules; their difference cannot be interpreted as a contradiction or a causal delay without field-level and case-level review.

observations.method: Official CFPB product-filtered API aggregation for student-loan complaints received in 2025; compare the company_response bucket with the separate timely bucket. The CFPB 2025 Consumer Response Annual Report provides an external rounded context of approximately 31% no timely response or no response for student loans.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; the year-over-year field movement may reflect servicing, routing, publication, coding, taxonomy, or index changes. The API field distinction is not itself an elapsed-time or borrower-outcome measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase may be a processing or classification change rather than a uniform deterioration in student-loan servicing; case-level notices, servicing transfer dates, payment status, and verified remedy are not present.

boundary: This is a field-definition and administrative-endpoint audit. It does not estimate student-loan borrower harm, elapsed response days, remedy adequacy, payment interruption, trust, switching, or causal servicing effects. The separate company_response and timely fields must be retained rather than collapsed.
